whatItDoes: Escapes raw text into a JSON string (quotes, backslashes, newlines, Unicode \uXXXX) and unescapes JSON strings back to raw. Handles nested JSON where a string contains stringified JSON.
whyItExists: Logs and API responses often contain nested JSON that must be pasted into code. Manual escaping is error-prone; this does it correctly per RFC 8259 and reverses it without losing Unicode.
whoShouldUse: Developers working with logs, API payloads, and code generation where JSON strings contain JSON.
useCases: Escape a multiline log line into a JSON string for a test fixture
Unescape a response field `\"{\\\"name\\\": \\\"a\\\"}\"` back to {"name": "a"}
Toggle Unicode escaping for \u00a0 vs raw characters
instructions: Paste text in Input, choose Escape (with options: wrap quotes, Unicode) or Unescape.
Escape uses JSON.stringify slicing; Unescape tries JSON.parse with quote wrapping then manual \n/\u fallback.
Copy the output from the preview (data-testid). No upload — pure string ops.
examples:
Input: Hello
World → Escape → "Hello
World" (with quotes) or Hello
World (without).
bestPractices: Use wrap quotes when pasting into code, without when storing as value
Enable Unicode escaping for ASCII-only transports
commonMistakes: Double-escaping — escape once, then paste; re-escaping will add extra backslashes
Expecting unescape to parse JSON objects — it returns text; use JSON Formatter to parse the result
faq: Is it the same as String Escape? JSON escaping is a subset (quotes/backslashes/controls); String Escape also handles HTML/URL.
Does it handle surrogate pairs? Yes — Unicode above U+FFFF is preserved or escaped as \uXXXX pairs.
Is it reversible? Escape then Unescape round-trips for valid JSON strings.
